_title: The councils Erik's play made, written down: the Radiant Council, the Harmonic Council, and Millbrook's elder panel
_why: Erik 2026-09-23: 'Can I write up the councils from your saves as content? — yes please.' Every body, person and standard here is read from the saves named in _fromPlay; nothing is invented except the strength numbers every power record needs, which follow the SNG-634 rules for their scale.

added.name: The Radiant Council

bodies.name: the Radiant Council
bodies.does: governs the Plateau under the High Luminary

bodies.name: the water-accountability office
bodies.does: surveys and records the valley's water

bodies.name: the Edge District accountability board
bodies.does: posts who is accountable for what

bodies.name: the deep stacks
bodies.does: the Council's locked archive; archivists see only approved fragments

holds.name: the Council's offices on the Edge District

added.wantsFromYou: Your discretion about anything you have seen at the river, and your help keeping the valley calm.
added.offersYou: Protection, passage anywhere on the Plateau, and a place on the right side of what is coming.
added.leverage: Its own archivists know the record they are shown has been cut. One of them, asked the right question at the right time, will say so.
added.whenBroken: The Plateau's hold on the valley slips, and the Harmonic Heights moves into every place the Council was buying.
secretsGM: It is the Patient Buyer: it buys the Roost's debts through the Undercount's counting-house, so its name is on nothing (Erik, 2026-09-23).

It has known longer than it admits what is waking under the Echo River, and built a secondary purification system in secret instead of stopping it. The system is incomplete and will not serve every household.
It keeps the full record of Verath-Sem, an Archive engineer of the Transition's close, in the locked stacks.
added.plainly: The governing council of the Radiant Plateau. It prizes clarity in public and keeps its own counsel in private.
added.descriptionSeed: The Radiant Council governs the Plateau under the High Luminary and speaks of clarity in everything. In private it plans a generation ahead and cuts its own archive to fit the plan. It is extending its reach over the unaligned valley one debt, one survey and one quiet favour at a time.
added.appearance: A council hall of photonic-crystal towers braiding sunlight into beams, light-guide streets below, an accountability board of lit panels in a public square

added.name: The Harmonic Council

bodies.name: the upper chamber
bodies.does: governs the Heights; moves by Priority Council packet and tells the terraces afterward

bodies.name: the Warden Council of the Lower Terrace
bodies.does: keeps the bulletin board, files notices, opens formal inquiries, and holds the sanction chain

bodies.name: the sanction chain
bodies.does: gate-senior clearance is what sanctions a Heights observer into the Disputed Zone

holds.name: the Warden Council's hall on the Lower Terrace

added.wantsFromYou: Word of anything you learn in the Disputed Zone, filed with the Warden Council, before the Plateau hears it.
added.offersYou: Sanction: a Heights observer with gate-senior clearance, which opens doors the Plateau's coin cannot.
added.leverage: The upper chamber keeps the Warden Council in the dark, and the wardens have noticed.
added.whenBroken: The terraces fall silent, and the Radiant Council inherits a valley with nobody left to balance it.
secretsGM: The upper chamber learned of the river's contamination before the Warden Council did, and has been sending internal packets about it overnight.
The sealed Resonance Halls need a reagent from the valley floor, and the couriers sent for it come back empty and will not say why.
added.plainly: The Harmonic Heights governs itself through a council: an upper chamber that decides and a Warden Council on the Lower Terrace that the public actually meets.
added.descriptionSeed: The Heights is governed from an upper chamber that moves by sealed Priority packet and explains itself later. Below it the Warden Council of the Lower Terrace posts notices, opens inquiries and holds the sanction chain, and knows less than it should about what the chamber above it has decided.
added.appearance: Terraced buildings of phononic crystal humming in the wind, tree-sized chimes, and on the lowest terrace a warden hall with a crowded public bulletin board

added.name: Millbrook's Elder Panel

bodies.name: the elder panel
bodies.does: five elders who meet in the common house and decide on the record
bodies._seatsFrom: Five elders (Usnea's run). Dresh anchors it; Elder Senna is a village elder (Cellaceron's run); Mara Wells is 'water-policy coordinator and elder' (Usnea's run); Dara Holt is recorded as 'Millbrook Council' (Silas's run). The fifth seat is not named in any save.

added.sanctionStandard: Mandate, not size. Millbrook sanctions a survey into the Disputed Zone only with two written settlement requests, a Heights-sanctioned observer with gate-senior clearance, and a named return date and return point.

contingents.what: Millbrook neighbours with what they own

added.wantsFromYou: Evidence laid on the common house table, and a request made in writing.
added.offersYou: Sanction the whole valley respects, because Millbrook gives it rarely and on the record.
added.leverage: Dresh moves on mandate, not size: bring the right written requests and the panel has to answer.
added.whenBroken: Millbrook stops being the place the valley brings things to be decided, and the cities decide instead.
added.plainly: Millbrook governs itself through an elder panel in its common house, led by Councilor Dresh. It decides slowly, in public, and on the record.
added.descriptionSeed: Five elders meet in Millbrook's common house around a long table where evidence is laid out and read aloud. Councilor Dresh leads by preference rather than command and asks for plain speech. Mara Wells coordinates the village's water policy from the panel, and Dara Holt, the Ditch-Mother, keeps the east channel. Once the panel formally accepts a thing it cannot pretend otherwise, which is why it accepts things slowly.
added.appearance: A long timber common house with a packed-earth floor, a long table covered in laid-out evidence, elders seated along one side, apple trees in the yard

partiesBefore.name: Renn
partiesBefore.what: lower-channel farmer, who cites precedent and compact

partiesBefore.note: their irrigation dispute came before the panel in Usnea's run; they are parties, not members

_notOnThePanel.aldric: Aldric, the smokehouse operator, appears only at an evening meeting Silas called at Pell's forge with Dara, Fendt, Mara and Calvar. That gathering was not the panel, and no save seats him. The fifth seat is open if Erik wants him in it.

added.name: Councilor Dresh
added.role: Councilor of Millbrook and head of its elder panel — leads the common house by preference rather than command, and asks what mandate a thing has before she asks how big it is
added.appearance: A broad-shouldered woman seated at the centre of the common house table, composed since dawn and there before anyone else.
added.voiceHints: Plain speech, and she asks the room for the same. Separates a smaller ask from a sanctioned one out loud, and only the second moves her.
added.wants: For Millbrook to act on what it can prove, under a mandate it can defend to every settlement it answers to.
added.fears: A panel that goes on pretending a thing is not happening because saying so would oblige it to act.
knowledge: What the valley's settlements have asked of Millbrook in writing, and what they have not

The terms on which Millbrook's panel will sanction a survey into the Disputed Zone: two written settlement requests, a Heights-sanctioned observer with gate-senior clearance, and a named return date and return point

reactsToReputation.any: hears you out at the table and asks what you want the panel to do
reactsToReputation.reliable: lets you speak before the other elders
reactsToReputation.reckless: asks who sanctioned it before anything else

questSeeds: Millbrook's elder panel sanctions nothing into the Disputed Zone without Dresh's three conditions
The panel answers to the settlements that write to it, and the cities have started writing
gear: a councilor's staff of plain ash
added.title: Councilor of Millbrook
added._domainsWhy: plain speech, what can be touched and proved, and mandate reasoned from premises

added.name: Elder Senna
added.role: Village elder of Millbrook and a voice on its common house panel — listens on her feet, cup set aside, watching your face
added.appearance: An older woman who stands to listen rather than sits, cup set down and forgotten, eyes on the speaker's face.
added.voiceHints: Says little until she has heard all of it, then says one thing.
added.wants: For Millbrook's people to be heard by the panel before the panel decides for them.
added.fears: The village deciding in a hurry what it cannot undo.
knowledge: Everyone in Millbrook, and which of them the panel has not yet heard

reactsToReputation.any: listens standing, and remembers exactly what you said

questSeeds: Senna holds a key someone left in her keeping
added.title: Elder of Millbrook
added._domainsWhy: the patience of the walled peace, feeling heard aloud, and a village she tends
added._levelWhy: §148: the tier is right (a ruling lord, a seated elder), so the level climbs to the tier's floor rather than the tier dropping.

added.name: Maren Vasse
added.role: Tuning-warden of the Harmonic Heights Lower Terrace — keeps the Warden Council's bulletin board, and decides what reaches the Council and when
added.appearance: A woman of about fifty with the Warden sash and deep acoustic calluses on both index fingers, standing watch by a bulletin board long enough for her tea to go cold.
added.voiceHints: Level and cataloguing, never alarmed. Pauses for calculation, not reluctance. Asks what goes to the Council before she decides how to log it.
added.wants: To know what the Warden Council should hear, and when, before she writes it down.
added.fears: The upper chamber moving on something before the Warden Council knows why.
knowledge: Every notice on the Lower Terrace bulletin board and who filed it
How to read relay traffic: three copies on one night with no stagger and a heavier seal is Council-internal
That Farren on the Second Terrace still consults for the Warden Council when nobody else can solve something

reactsToReputation.any: logs what you tell her, and asks what else she should know
reactsToReputation.reliable: backs you, on the condition that the Council can reach you

questSeeds: The Warden Council logged a missing apprentice as unsanctioned solo practice and gave it low priority
Priority Council packets are moving overnight and nobody has told the Lower Terrace why
gear: a tuning fork of dark crystal
added.title: Tuning-Warden of the Lower Terrace
added._registryName: Maren — the save's registry calls her by her given name alone; four characters on this device have met a Maren. The record now carries a family name and a title so she is never only 'Maren' again.
added._domainsWhy: what is so, logged in order, kept calm

added.name: Farren Quire
added.role: Retired acoustic geometry specialist of the Harmonic Heights Second Terrace — still consults for the Warden Council when nobody else can solve something
added.appearance: A lean man past sixty in a heavy work-tunic, resonance calluses on both forearms, hair damp from the basin, dressed for work and not for company.
added.voiceHints: Difficult and thorough. Wants to know why before he will touch a thing, and pushes until he gets a real answer.
added.wants: A problem nobody else on the Heights can solve.
added.fears: Being consulted to confirm an answer someone has already chosen.
knowledge: The acoustic geometry of the Heights' terraces and what their structures are tuned to

reactsToReputation.any: asks why you want to know before he tells you anything

questSeeds: Farren can read a terminal direction from a resonance instrument, if someone gives him a reason
gear: geometry instruments in a worn case
a work-tunic scored by resonance burns
added._playNote: The registry records him as a man; one scene line said 'she'. The registry wins.
added.title: Acoustic Geometer of the Second Terrace, retired
added._domainsWhy: geometry as pattern, instruments, and reasoning that wants the why first

added.name: Sorel Halloran
added.role: Archivist of the Radiant Council's water-accountability office — surveys the valley's water and knows exactly which fragments of the record the Council lets archivists see
added.appearance: A woman of about sixty in undyed wool, a Plateau optical-fibre collar worn plain and small, a weight-distributed satchel, and a photonic instrument she reads the river with.
added.voiceHints: Steady, precise, and careful about what she says of the Council. When she chooses to say it, she says it plainly.
added.wants: For the water record to say what the water actually does.
added.fears: Being the only one who knows what the Council chose.
knowledge: The Council's water surveys and where their markers were set
The three approved fragments archivists may read about the Archive engineers of the Transition's close
What 'instrumental' means when the Council uses it instead of a name

reactsToReputation.any: measures you before she trusts you with anything the Council has not approved
reactsToReputation.honest: tells you what the survey found

questSeeds: The Council's water office ordered survey markers moved before an archivist could find what they marked

added.title: Archivist of the Water-Accountability Office

added.name: Dara Holt
added.title: the Ditch-Mother
added.role: Senior east-channel irrigator of Millbrook, called the Ditch-Mother, and a member of Millbrook's elder panel
added.appearance: A composed woman standing at her own door before the frost has melted, a mug held in both hands.
added.voiceHints: Does her accounting fast and quiet, then waits. Will not say a theory aloud until someone else has confirmed it.
added.wants: The east channel running clean and on time, and the panel acting on the water before the water acts on Millbrook.
added.fears: Being the one who said it first and being wrong in front of the whole panel.
knowledge: Every sluice, sleeve and blank on Millbrook's east channel, and when each last failed

reactsToReputation.any: hears you out at her door and gives nothing away
reactsToReputation.reliable: tells you what she has not told the panel
